there is a reduction in the number and size of the islets and a reduction in the percent of the insulin cells.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the histopathology of the islets in FCPD is similar to that in Type I diabetes, but with a lesser degree of severity.
there is a reduction of islet cells in FCPD patients, but some of the islets show hyperplasia and some of them are hyperplastic.
FCPD is characterized by a spectrum of pancreatic changes ranging from atrophy to fibrosis, ductal degeneration and islet cell hyperplasia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FCPD is a disease with a wide spectrum of changes in the pancreatic parenchyma.
the islets in FCPD patients are altered in a manner that is different from other forms of diabetes mellitus.
FCPD is a heterogenous disease, and the histopathology varies from moderate atrophy, fibrous replacement to severe atrophy.
